paper_title: Joint Detection of Fraud and Concept Drift inOnline Conversations with   LLM-Assisted Judgment
caption: A runtime comparison between our ensemble model and various LLM models on the SEconvo dataset
model_annotation: The bar chart, titled “Runtime Comparison of Models in Streaming Environment,” visually compares the inference runtime (in seconds) of “Our Joint Framework” against four prominent large language models — ChatGPT, DeepSeek, LLaMA, and Claude — on the SEconvo dataset, as referenced in the paper “Joint Detection of Fraud and Concept Drift in Online Conversations with LLM-Assisted Judgment.” The vertical axis represents runtime in seconds, ranging from 0 to 400 with major gridlines every 50 seconds. The horizontal axis lists the five models, with “Our Joint Framework” shown as a single dark green bar (77 seconds), and the four LLMs shown as light blue bars: ChatGPT (190 seconds), DeepSeek (365 seconds), LLaMA (172 seconds), and Claude (243 seconds). A legend in the upper left corner distinguishes “Our Joint Framework” (dark green) from “LLM Models” (light blue). The chart clearly illustrates that “Our Joint Framework” achieves significantly lower runtime compared to all tested LLMs, with DeepSeek being the slowest at 365 seconds and LLaMA the fastest among LLMs at 172 seconds. Each bar is labeled with its exact runtime value above it, and the bars are arranged in order of model type rather than runtime magnitude.
